issues.on_page: Loan payments 52,472 (LB840 loan payments, Sales Tax Fund p16)
issues.issue: These are repayments on LB840 loans the city made (notes receivable on p1), mostly principal coming back, so arguably not revenue. 'other' with review is defensible, but a person may want them treated as other financing. Same for detail[132].

The label says reimbursement (category reimbursements/refunds), but it comes from the city's Community Redevelopment Authority component unit. The Statement of Activities p3 shows it as capital grants and contributions under Public works. Either way it is a judgment call. Same for detail[127] (county/other local governments).

issues.on_page: Cemetery department; statement p6 counts General Fund Public works 77,919 = Cemetery
issues.issue: The category follows the rule (cemetery is health/welfare), but the detail function split no longer ties to the statement's Public works line. The receipts statement line (disbursements[3]) has a review note, but these detail lines don't.

issues.extracted: department function (general government / public safety / culture/recreation / streets/highways)
issues.on_page: Capital outlay 73,378 / 20,480 / 7,385 / 5,274 (General Fund) and 15,357 (Street); Debt service Principal 18,156, Interest 168 (Police)
issues.issue: Statement p6 reports these on its own Capital outlay (106,517 General + 15,357 Street), Principal payments on debt and Interest lines, not under the functions. Giving them the department function means detail totals by function won't tie to the statement (e.g. General Fund public safety detail 745,037 vs statement 700,959). Categories capital outlay / debt service principal / debt service interest would tie.

issues.on_page: Transportation 8,795 (Police); also Library 7, Park 1,907, Cemetery 2,098, Fire 890
issues.issue: For police, park, cemetery and fire, 'Transportation' is more likely vehicle fuel/operation (fuel) than training and travel. This is a judgment call.

issues.on_page: Transfer to Imperial Manor (220,000) General Fund; Transfers to Imperial Manor (60,572) Light Fund p10
issues.issue: Imperial Manor is a component unit, not a city fund, so these are one-sided transfers to an outside entity. They may really be operating subsidies (spending). The existing decision_needed entry covers only the transfers-in netting; it doesn't ask whether the 280,572 paid to Imperial Manor should count as transfers or as spending.
